newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse to consider president candidates.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse to consider president candidates.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) board of governors is expected to meet on Wednesday to consider a replacement for former PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas who quit abruptly at the weekend, a board member said.

"We are going to meet tomorrow and thrash out this issue. We will make a list of possible candidates for the presidency and later present them to the members for approval," Harry Liu, PSE board member and treasurer, told Reuters on Tuesday.

Nanagas resigned on Saturday five months into his three-year term because of irreconcilable differences with his staff, the exchange said. Some officials said the disputes included the high salaries paid to recent recruits.

"The candidate should be a great manager and one who will be able to balance the interest of the members, the requirements of the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) and public interest, as well," Filomeno Francisco, PSE governor, told Reuters.
Both governors could not provide details of the list of candidates. Wilson Sy, chairman of the PSE, said in a statement on Monday the bourse was already reviewing a list of candidates.
A source familiar with the situation said five names were on the list, including people who had previously been considered for the president's job.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay has given the stock exchange a month to name the new president.
In the meantime, the SEC would suspend a decision on the bourse's application for self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status, Yasay told reporters on Monday.
At present, PSE chief operating officer Rafael Llave oversees the daily operations at the exchange, the two governors said.
Nanagas' departure followed high-level resignations at the bourse last week for reasons not yet clear.
Market speculation pinned the exodus to a revolt against tough reforms expected to be put in place by the former president.
Last October after Nanagas joined the PSE, the bourse members voted in favour of reforms aimed at making the market more transparent and seat-holders more accountable.
While Nanagas himself played down the resignations of the senior officials, saying they had left for "greener pastures", he said he had tried to raise standards at the exchange.
"Everyone knows that the PSE operated like a membership club and that the key challenge was to professionalize," Nanagas said in a statement faxed to news organisations on Tuesday.
In the meantime, the vacancy should not hurt stock trading, Liu said.

"I don't think that the search for the presidency will affect negatively the daily activities at the bourse. It doesn't mean that when the company president is not around, the company won't survive," Liu said.
The source close to the situation disagreed. "In the short run it does not (have an impact)," he said. "But in the long run, if it isn't solved, there will be a reduction in credibility."
